contract.label: Toggle
contract.summary: A two-state button that holds a pressed/on state.

parts.name: Toggle
parts.description: Pressable button toggling a pressed/on state.

props.name: surface
props.description: What the toggle sits on — default inside a card, sheet, dialog or table row, where an outline toggle rests clear so the surface shows through; page straight on the shell's muted content area, where it rests and hovers like an outline Button so a toolbar reads as one surface. Only the outline variant has a face to swap; the ghost default needs nothing on either.

rules: **Pick the surface by what is underneath.** An outline toggle placed straight on the shell's `muted` content area — a toolbar, a filter row — takes `surface="page"`, which rests and hovers like an outline Button (`outline-surface`, `outline-hover`), so the row reads as one surface. Inside a `card`, `sheet`, `dialog` or table row it keeps `default`. The ghost `default` variant has no resting face on either, exactly like a ghost Button, so `surface` leaves it alone.

A `toggle-group` placed straight on the shell's `muted` content area — an interval or view switcher in a toolbar — takes `surface="page"`, so it rests and hovers like the outline Buttons beside it. A connected group (`spacing={0}`) puts the face on its outline items; a spaced group puts it on its frame and the items inside stay `default`. Inside a `card`, `sheet`, `dialog` or table row it keeps `default`.
examples: `<Toggle variant="outline" surface="page" aria-label="Compare to last period">Compare</Toggle>` beside `<Button variant="outline">` in a toolbar on the page body.
`<ToggleGroup variant="outline" spacing={0} surface="page" defaultValue={["hourly"]}>` in a filter row on the page body.
antiPatterns: An outline toggle on the muted page body given `bg-background`, `bg-card` or `bg-white` instead of `surface="page"` — in dark mode `background` is darker than `card`, so the toggle sinks below the cards beside it.

A toggle group on the muted page body given `bg-background`, `bg-card` or `bg-white` instead of `surface="page"` — in dark mode `background` is darker than `card`, so the group sinks below the cards beside it.
